brief: LCX Services: businesses everywhere cold business email is allowed, offered every LCX service in one email with the services deck attached (docs/LCX Services.pdf; the deck is docs/decks/LCX Services - pitch deck.pdf). The owner, 2026-10-06: "i wanna build outreach a single one offering all these services", then "it should generate the leads on its own for the people and businesses we can pitch the services to" and "like we source leads for us production houses i want leads to come like that". So it harvests by itself every Friday, like the production houses: the buyers of each service (config audiences) from Wikidata and OpenStreetMap, through the promote chain, an address from the business itself or its own website, and a draft a person approves. Apollo is not used for it; the Apollo search page stays for adding a lead by hand.

geography.guidance: The owner, 2026-10-06: "Everywhere allowed" -- every country except those whose law needs consent before a cold business email: Canada (CASL), Germany and Austria (UWG), Italy, the same set as LCX Clipping. A company is left out only on evidence: Wikidata says its only country is one of them, or the city it was found in is. english_markets earns a small bonus (score_modifiers.english_market) because the email and the deck are in English; it never leaves anyone out.

retail chain, department store chain, supermarket chain, fashion house, online shop
bank, insurance company, asset management company
film production company, television production company, animation studio, advertising agency

audiences_guidance: Who buys which of the 18 services on docs/LCX Services.pdf, and where they are found (tools/discover_lcx_services.py). Every email offers every service; the audience decides who is found, what the lead says it fits (why_fit, Pitch first) and audience_fit in the rubric: 1.0 where the sheet's services fit directly, 0.5 where the sale is slower (banks and insurers, attractions). wikidata entries match a class (P31) or an industry (P452), as Wikidata items (QIDs); osm entries are OpenStreetMap tag pairs. Add an audience, a class or a tag here and the next harvest finds it.

discovery.guidance: Each Friday's refresh stages up to 600 new companies from Wikidata (an equal share for each audience, at most per_audience; 10 to 5,000 people first, and within that English-speaking markets first, since the email and the deck are in English) and up to 600 local businesses from OpenStreetMap (cities_per_run cities, a different few each week). The site pass after it reads up to 600 websites, so a week's harvest is read the week it arrives. skip_known_elsewhere: a business already a lead of another project is not staged here, so nobody is pitched by two projects from the same address.

osm_discovery.guidance: OpenStreetMap's Overpass API, the endpoints tried in turn (the main one did not answer from the office on 2026-10-06; a mirror did). Each run takes discovery.osm.cities_per_run of these cities, a different few each ISO week, and asks each audience's tags within radius_m of the centre, for places that publish a website or an email address. Coverage follows the map's volunteers: on 2026-10-06 London had about 1,400 cafes with a website or address, Mumbai 26. Cities in English-speaking business markets only, since the email and the deck are in English; add a city here and it joins the rotation. Data (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL, recorded on each lead it found.

rubric.label: Someone to write to: a named person (full) or the business's own published address (half)
rubric.guidance: 1.0 a named person in a deciding role with their own address (the site pass, or a person); 0.5 a business address (info@, hello@) the business publishes on OpenStreetMap, on Wikidata or on its own site (tools/enrich_lcx_services.py, enrich_contacts). Half the points on purpose: a lead nobody can be written to tops out at 50 (54 with the English bonus) and never crosses the auto-shortlist line at 55, so nothing is shortlisted that cannot be drafted.

rubric.label: A buyer the services fit directly
rubric.guidance: From the lead's audience (config audiences, fit): 1.0 brands, retailers, real estate, hotels and short stays, publishers, studios and agencies, schools, cafes, salons and gyms, independent shops; 0.5 banks and insurers, attractions, where the sale is slower.

rubric.label: An established business
rubric.guidance: 1.0 a company notable enough for Wikidata, or a local business that publishes its website and its phone or opening hours; 0.5 a local business with less on record.

rubric.label: The size that buys this and answers a cold email
rubric.guidance: 1.0 at 10 to 5,000 people, or an independent local business; 0.5 at 1-9 or 5,001-50,000 people; 0 above 50,000 (a procurement process, not a reply). Unverified (0) when Wikidata gives no headcount.

score_modifiers.label: BONUS: an English-speaking business market
score_modifiers.guidance: The email and the deck are in English. 1.0 in geography.english_markets, 0 in any other allowed country, absent when the country is unknown. Four points: enough to order two equal leads, never enough to shortlist a lead nobody can be written to.

gates.label: Not in a country where cold business email needs consent
gates.guidance: Fires only on confirmed evidence of a disallowed country (geography.disallowed_countries). Unknown always passes.

gates.label: Not a company of over 100,000 people
gates.guidance: Set from Wikidata's headcount. Companies that size buy through procurement and have in-house teams for all of this; a cold email from LCX is not how they buy. Unknown passes.

gates.label: Some way to reach them: a website or an address
gates.guidance: Fires only on an explicit false. The harvest stages nothing without a website or a published address, so this is a guard.

auto_shortlist.guidance: Like the production houses: every lead in To review scoring above 55 is shortlisted by the last step of the promote chain, and a shortlisted lead with an address is drafted within minutes. 55 is just above what a lead nobody can be written to can score (50, 54 with the English bonus), so everything shortlisted can be drafted. Shortlisting sends nothing: every email is approved by a person. Leads at or below the line stay in To review, where a person can shortlist one by hand.

enrichment.guidance: An address comes from the business itself: the one it publishes on OpenStreetMap or Wikidata (tools/enrich_lcx_services.py), else its own website, read politely with robots.txt honoured (enrich_contacts_lcxs, tools/enrich_sitescrape.py). Never LinkedIn. enabled is the Apollo gate (tools/enrich_apollo.py) and is false: the owner, 2026-10-06, 'forget apollo for a sec'. Apollo enrichment can be turned on for this project later with a weekly credit budget, as for US Production Houses.

sources.name: Wikidata (companies by class and industry)
sources.detail: tools/discover_lcx_services.py --source wikidata: operating companies with an official website in each audience's classes and industries, not only in a consent-law country. CC0, free, no key.

sources.name: OpenStreetMap (local businesses around a city)
sources.detail: tools/discover_lcx_services.py --source osm: independent cafes, salons, gyms, shops, estate agents, guest houses, schools and attractions that publish a website or an email address, a few cities a week. ODbL, free, no key.

sources.name: Apollo.io search (by hand)
sources.detail: The Apollo search page, for adding a lead by hand. Saving a person reveals them: 1 credit each. Not part of the weekly harvest.

self_exclusion.guidance: TVF and its affiliates never enter the lead pool, from any source. Domains match on the host or a subdomain, name patterns as whole words.

templates.subject: 18 things LCX can do for {{company}}
templates.body:
Hi {{greeting_name}},

I'm writing from LCX. We work in three areas, and at least one of them should be useful to {{company}}. Our services deck is attached.

If one fits, reply with its name and I'll send examples.

{{footer}}
templates.guidance: The owner's choice, 2026-10-06: a short email with the services deck attached as a PDF, in the wording the owner approved. {{greeting_name}} is the person's first name when one is known, else 'there'. The deck in attachments goes with every email from this template; the sender checks it is the same file that was drafted and approved, and holds the email back if it changed.

batch_approval.guidance: Every draft here comes from one template with no model-written sentence, so they may be approved together: select them in Drafts, read the random sample the server draws (at least sample_min, or sample_fraction of the batch, whichever is more), tick each, approve. Every draft is checked first (no {{placeholder}}, no SET_ME, a valid address, a sendable company, the deck present).

outreach.guidance: The owner, 2026-10-06: one email offering every LCX service, with the services deck attached, to the businesses the weekly harvest finds. Like US Production Houses: a shortlisted lead with an address is drafted by itself from the one template, a person approves it (one at a time, or a spot-checked batch), and it goes from that person's own Gmail (send_from approver, linked by the owner with tools/users.py gmail), inside that address's daily limit, which it shares with every other project. One first email per company and per inbox; no follow-ups. Not paused: the owner chose 'send once approved'. Replies land in Outreach -> Replies.

apollo.guidance: The search page's settings, the same as Universal (see config/segment.universal.json): people search 0 credits, company search 1 credit per page, bulk_match 1 credit per person Apollo has data for. max_reveal_per_save caps one save; the page asks before every save that costs credits.
